Defense

Seth Jones, D, Florida Panthers (2.31 FPPG, 30.1% available): Jones has heated up in a hurry, with seven points in his past three games, and only 14 skaters have more fantasy points across the past two weeks. With Aleksander Barkov out until at least late November, the Panthers need offense from somewhere, and Jones is a fixture on the top power-play unit with five points on the advantage already. He's still available in nearly a third of leagues, and that shouldn't last.

Neal Pionk, D, Winnipeg Jets (2.12 FPPG, 72.0% available): With Josh Morrissey out until at least Nov. 1, Pionk has stepped into top-pair minutes and the top power-play unit for the Jets. Five points in his past three games are the flashy part, but the real foundation is 24-plus minutes a night and a steady stream of hits and blocks, which account for nearly half of his fantasy points. He's available in nearly three-quarters of leagues.

Travis Sanheim, D, Philadelphia Flyers (1.70 FPPG, 31.2% available): Injuries to Rasmus Ristolainen and Cam York have pushed Sanheim's ice time to a staggering 27:32 per game over his past three, and 21 blocked shots have done most of the fantasy work. He's not on the power play and his pair with Oliver Bonk is 0-4 on goals at 5-on-5, so this is a play for leagues that reward blocks. Two of the Flyers' three games land on light nights.

See also:

Alexandre Carrier, D, Montreal Canadiens (1.70 FPPG, 93.3% available)

Martin Fehervary, D, Washington Capitals (1.90 FPPG, 71.4% available)

Tyler Kleven, D, Ottawa Senators (2.03 FPPG, 78.3% available)

Justin Faulk, D, Detroit Red Wings (1.51 FPPG, 34.2% available)

Goaltenders

Jet Greaves, G, Columbus Blue Jackets (2.35 FPP60, 49.5% available): Cam Talbot has taken three of the past seven starts, but Greaves still holds the edge in the Blue Jackets crease after posting 2.06 FPPG across 55 games last season. This week is the downside: only two games, and neither is a top-10 matchup for goalies.

Dylan Garand, G, New York Rangers (4.20 FPP60, 45.4% available): With Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo on IR until at least Nov. 9, Garand's only competition is Spencer Martin, who hasn't started any of the Rangers' past 10 games. Three wins and a .927 save percentage through six games is a solid opening, and he's still available in nearly half of leagues. None of this week's three opponents offers a particularly favorable matchup for goalies, but volume is the draw.

Lukas Dostal, G, Anaheim Ducks (0.49 FPP60, 58.7% available): It's been a rough start for Dostal, and that's exactly why he's sitting on the wire in most leagues. The schedule makes a strong case for buying low anyway. The Ducks have four games and the second-best goalie schedule of the week, including the Rangers and Devils, both favorable matchups for fantasy goalies. Even a share of that crease is worth chasing.

See also:

Pyotr Kochetkov, G, Carolina Hurricanes (4.08 FPP60, 49.6% available)

Devon Levi, G, Edmonton Oilers (2.50 FPP60, 68.7% available)

Jacob Markstrom, G, Florida Panthers (2.43 FPP60, 38.4% available)

Juuse Saros, G, Nashville Predators (1.78 FPP60, 31.6% available)

Short-term streamers

Gabriel Landeskog, LW, Colorado Avalanche (1.74 FPPG, 73.2% available): The Avalanche are this week's top team for streaming, and Landeskog is an easy way in. He's on the second line with Nazem Kadri and Brock Nelson, has three points in his past three games and chips in hits. With three of Colorado's four games on light nights, he can slot into a daily lineup with little competition.

Blake Coleman, RW, Minnesota Wild (1.46 FPPG, 43.0% available): Coleman has gone quiet with no points in his past three games, but the schedule is too good to ignore. The Wild play four times, and their opponents combine for the friendliest slate of the week for top-six forwards, with two bottom-10 penalty kills on the trip. Now skating on the second line with Ryan Hartman and Bobby Brink, he also adds hits (18 so far) to cover the quiet nights.

Jonas Brodin, D, Minnesota Wild (1.49 FPPG, 96.3% available): Brodin is almost purely a blocked-shots play, with 22 of them making up nearly all of his 13.4 fantasy points. But he's skating 86% of his even-strength time next to Quinn Hughes while Jared Spurgeon and Brock Faber are out, and the Wild's four opponents combine for the fourth-friendliest slate for top-four defenders. That pairing may not survive Spurgeon's return, so treat this as a one-week deep-league rental.

Josh Manson, D, Colorado Avalanche (1.77 FPPG, 74.3% available): Like Landeskog, Manson is a vehicle for the Avalanche schedule: four games, three of them on light nights, against opponents who combine for the third-friendliest slate for top-four defenders. Playing on the top pair with Brent Burns, he gets most of his value from hits and blocks, which account for more than half of his fantasy points.

Alexander Wennberg, C, San Jose Sharks (1.06 FPPG, 86.0% available): Wennberg's slow start is a far cry from last season's 1.75 FPPG, but the role points to a turnaround. He's up to 21-plus minutes a night over his past three games, including more than five minutes on the top power-play unit, and his new line with Tyler Toffoli and Mason Marchment is controlling 61.9% of the shot attempts. The Sharks' four opponents combine for the second-friendliest slate for top-six forwards.

John Gibson, G, Detroit Red Wings (-0.61 FPP60, 41.2% available): The Red Wings have the third-best goalie schedule of the week, and all three of their games are top-10 matchups for fantasy goalies, including the Canucks (second) and Flames (first). With no bad draws on the slate, whichever games Gibson gets should be good ones.

stories.headline: Griezmann has 2 goals, 1 assist for Orlando City in 4-1 win over DC United
stories.summary: Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- - Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.

Griezmann has 12 goals and seven assists in 14 MLS appearances and is the first player in league history with a goal contribution in 12 of his first 14 career games.

Marco Pasalić scored a stoppage-time goal for Orlando (12-13-5). Maxime Crépeau had three saves.

Tai Baribo converted from the penalty spot in first-half stoppage time for D.C. (7-10-12).

Ojeda, just inside the top of the 18-yard box, chipped a first-touch pass over four defenders to a charging Griezmann on the give-and-go for a first-touch finish from 7 yards out to make it 1-0 in the 15th minute.

Ojeda flicked a back-heel volley, off a feed from Griezmann, past goalkeeper Sean Johnson and inside the left post to give Orlando a two-goal lead in the 22nd.

Griezmann intercepted a misplayed pass by Kye Rowles in D.C.'s defensive third, took two dribbles and rolled a shot into the net to make it 3-1 in the 50th minute.

Johnson finished with three saves.

Up next D.C.: Plays Wednesday at Cincinnati.

Orlando: Hosts New York City next Saturday.

stories.headline: PSG match a test to show what Barcelona can do - Hansi Flick
stories.summary: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick challenged his players to show they can compete with Europe's best by beating PSG on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick challenged his players to show they can compete with Europe's best by beating Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday to extend their perfect start to the season.

Barça have won 11 matches in a row to kick off the new campaign, scoring 48 goals in the process, but that streak will be put to the test by back-to-back European champions PSG at the Parc des Princes.

Both teams have won their opening two games in the Champions League, although PSG's 4-2 win at Manchester City last week demonstrated they are still the team to beat in Europe.

"It will be a good test for us to show how far we are," Flick said in the pre-game news conference on Monday.

"I would like my team to play with confidence, play brave and, of course, play together as a team. We did it in the last 11 games; now we play against, if you see the last two years, the best team in the world.

"For us, it's a good opportunity to show our level, show what we can do and [see] what we have to improve. After this match, we will also know a lot of things."

The two teams met in the league phase last season, with PSG running out 2-1 winners in Barcelona.

Flick acknowledges the French champions remain the more mature side, but feels Barça, who have not won the Champions League since 2015, pose a completely different proposition to the team they were 12 months ago.

"For me, last season was a difficult year, a difficult season," he added.

"This year, we play from the beginning the style we want and expect to play. We have confidence with the ball and create a lot of chances... I think it's totally different.

"But this is just one game against a fantastic team with an excellent coach in Luis Enrique. They have more maturity [than us]. The last years, they improve together as a team, what they achieve together is amazing."

Flick confirmed that Raphinha, who returned from a hamstring injury as a substitute in the weekend's win at Real Betis, "can start" in Paris, but lamented the team's lack of defenders.

Andreas Christensen, Jules Koundé and Eric García will all miss the game, with Gerard Martín also a minor doubt after picking up a knock against Betis.

Pau Cubarsí, therefore, is the only centre-back guaranteed to be available for the tie, although Flick says he has other options in the squad.

"Rodri can play there, also Frenkie [de Jong] and Álex Campos is with us from the B team," the German coach said.

"I am positive, I hope that everything goes well. It's not the best moment for us, but we have to accept it."

stories.headline: Jasmine Jasudavicius outpoints Erin Blanchfield at UFC Fight Night
stories.summary: Jasmine Jasudavicius stated her case as a contender in the UFC women's featherweight division, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas to win by unanimous decision.
stories.body:
Instability and opportunity permeate the UFC women's flyweight division, which crowned a new champion two weeks ago and has a former two-time champ lurking in the wings while healing from injury. Several other title hopefuls have been jostling to position themselves to go for the gold.

Jasmine Jasudavicius seized the opportunity to make her presence felt among the leading contenders Saturday, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas in a clash of top-10 125-pounders to win by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton, Alberta.

The fight was the co-main event of a card headlined by Mike Malott's explosive knockout win over Joaquin Buckley. Malott, who like Jasudavicius is from Ontario and had the crowd firmly behind him, landed a knee to the chin that crumbled Buckley, who is No. 8 in the ESPN welterweight rankings and lost his third in a row.

"Hey, guys, I might be soft-spoken," Malott said afterward, "but I'm f---ing hard-hitting."

Malott's knockout came at 2 minutes, 32 seconds of the second round and put a ferocious cap on an event that tied a UFC record with 12 finishes (seven knockouts, five submissions). The other modern-era fight card with a dozen finishes was UFC Fight Night in Belgrade, Serbia, on Aug. 1.

Nevertheless, it was the night's lone bout to go the distance that had the highest stakes. Jasudavicius, No. 8 in the ESPN women's flyweight rankings, pulled off the upset against third-ranked Blanchfield, who came in situated behind only injured former champion Valentina Shevchenko and new titlist Natalia Silva. Blanchfield is also No. 9 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound top 10.

Jasudavicius (16-4) surely elevated her standing in the 125-pound hierarchy with a robust performance that produced her second straight victory.

Both women came in touted as elite grapplers, and Jasudavicius proved to be a step ahead by repeatedly taking the fight to the ground (five takedowns) and threatening submissions from dominant positions for long stretches of the first two rounds.

"I love grappling," she said. "I understand it. I'm pretty good at it. And I like to show what I've got."

Jasudavicius showed enough to impress the judges, getting the nod on all three scorecards (29-28, 29-28, 29-28). The announcement of the verdict drew a roar from the crowd, which was enthusiastically behind the 37-year-old competing in her home country.

"To be able to fight in Canada, you hear the crowd, man. We're about it," Jasudavicius said.

Jasudavicius and Malott were among a dozen Canadian fighters on the card who went a combined 5-7.

Jasudavicius' victory might not put her in position for an immediate title shot, but she has her sights on a future meeting with the new champion, who defeated her by decision in 2022 in her second UFC fight.

"I want to cross paths with Natalia Silva again," Jasudavicius said. "We had a little bit of history before, so it would be an epic story."

For Blanchfield (14-3), the defeat halted a two-fight winning streak. She outlanded Jasudavicius 62-43 in significant strikes, but the author of five UFC submissions never could get her ground game going. Jasudavicius put Blanchfield on the defensive the whole fight with nearly eight minutes of control time.

stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 18th round.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the United States Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

Circuit: Circuit of the Americas; Austin, Texas

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2012

Lap record: 1:36.169, Charles Leclerc (2019)

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Most wins: Lewis Hamilton with six (2007, 2012, 2014-2017) Other winners from the current grid are Verstappen (2021-2023, 2025) and Leclerc (2024).

Most poles: Hamilton (2007, 2016-2018) is tied with Michael Schumacher (2000-2002, 2006) on four. Other pole sitters from the current grid are Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2022), Leclerc (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Weather forecast

The weather for the United States Grand Prix is expected to be light rain with a gentle breeze throughout the course of the weekend, with highs of 32°C.

What happened last time out?
Verstappen edged out Norris to take an imperious pole position by 0.291 seconds.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.
